claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Nevada
claims.text: Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency, effective August 10 and remaining in effect through August 17, 2026 unless terminated sooner, for areas of Washoe County and the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony impacted by the Bug and Fred Mountain Fires; as of that evening the fires had burned more than 16,000 acres and more than 6,000 people had been evacuated, with thousands more residents in warning zones. The declaration directs all state agencies to work through the Nevada Emergency Operations Center to supplement local efforts, and the Federal Emergency Management Agency separately authorized the use of federal funds to assist Nevada in combating the Bug Fire.

As of 8/14/2026: Bug Fire 88,422 acres, 31% contained, started 8 August 2026 at 3:30 PM, 591 personnel assigned; Stallion Fire 40,698 acres, 44% contained, started 10 August 2026, 322 personnel assigned; combined 93,367 acres and 717 personnel. Location given as 3 miles south of Hallelujah Junction, California. Both fires are attributed to human causes, burning in tall grass, brush and pinyon-juniper fuels. The 14 August 2026 update notes: "Wetting Rains Aid Firefighting Resources Increasing Containment," with thunderstorms bringing cooler temperatures and higher humidity.

InciWeb (update posted 15 August 2026, 7:49 PM): Bug Fire is 93,381 acres and 58% contained (717 personnel); Stallion Fire is 40,691 acres and 81% contained (282 personnel); combined-incident totals are 94,105 acres and 84% of the perimeter contained, with 849 total personnel assigned. No deaths, injuries or structures-destroyed figures are listed.

description: The Bug Fire ignited on 8 August 2026 near Hallelujah Junction on the California-Nevada border and, driven by strong winds and dry vegetation, grew rapidly into Washoe County, Nevada, threatening communities including Cold Springs and the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony; the neighboring Stallion Fire ignited nearby on 10 August. Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency on 10 August, with more than 16,000 acres burned and more than 6,000 people evacuated at that time, and FEMA authorized federal funds to assist Nevada in combating the Bug Fire. Both fires are attributed to human causes, burning in tall grass, brush and pinyon-juniper fuels. Aided by wetting rains, containment advanced quickly: as of 15 August 2026 the combined incident stood at 94,105 acres with 84% of the perimeter contained (Bug Fire 93,381 acres at 58% contained; Stallion Fire 40,691 acres at 81%), with 849 personnel assigned. No deaths, injuries or destroyed structures have been reported.

impact.summary: Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo's 10 August 2026 state-of-emergency declaration reported more than 16,000 acres burned and more than 6,000 people evacuated from areas of Washoe County and the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony, with thousands more residents in warning zones. As of 15 August 2026 the combined Bug and Stallion incident stood at 94,105 acres with 84% of the perimeter contained (Bug Fire 58%, Stallion Fire 81%) and 849 personnel assigned; no deaths, injuries or structure losses have been reported.

InciWeb reported the Bug Fire at 88,422 acres and 31% contained and the Stallion Fire at 40,698 acres and 44% contained, a combined 93,367 acres with 717 personnel assigned, with wetting rains from thunderstorms bringing cooler temperatures and higher humidity that aided containment.

Governor Lombardo declared a state of emergency for areas of Washoe County and the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony, effective through 17 August 2026 unless terminated sooner, citing more than 16,000 acres burned and more than 6,000 people evacuated, with thousands more residents in warning zones; FEMA separately authorized federal funds to assist Nevada in combating the Bug Fire.
